titleZh: Sabanto将自动驾驶与Precision Planting 20|20系统集成，实现无人播种
summaryZh: 美国公司Sabanto宣布其自动驾驶系统已支持搭载Precision Planting Gen 3 20|20系统的播种机，结合改装拖拉机可实现无人播种，农户通过远程界面监控作业。系统逐行读取播种数据并与设定容差比对，超差即暂停，旨在解决自主播种中“信任播种机”的核心难题。该集成计划于2027年种植季推出，对现有Sabanto用户免费。
featuredReason: 该报道展示了自动驾驶农机与主流播种监控系统集成的务实路径，其“超差即暂停”的容错逻辑和远程诊断思路对智慧畜牧中自动化设备的异常处理与远程监管具有直接借鉴意义。
contentFull:
Sabanto links autonomy to Precision Planting’s 20|20 for unmanned planting

 06-11 | Autonomous vehicles | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

Sabanto says growers told it that the driving itself was not the difficult part of autonomous planting. The harder question was whether they could trust the planter without someone watching it. Photos: Sabanto

US company Sabanto has announced support for planters equipped with the Precision Planting Gen 3 20|20 system. Combined with a Sabanto-retrofitted tractor, the setup allows autonomous planting without an operator in the seat. Growers can supervise the work remotely through Sabanto’s Vehicle Mission Control (vMC) interface. Support is planned for the 2027 growing season.

“I want to see a future where technology in agriculture is more open”, says Sabanto founder and CEO Craig Rupp. He compares it to a printer: you connect a USB cable, and within minutes it works. In agriculture, he says, getting any planter and any tractor to work together is far less simple. Rupp presents the integration as a step in that direction.

Sabanto says growers told it that the driving itself was not the difficult part of autonomous planting. The harder question was whether they could trust the planter without someone watching it. Planting is time-critical, with narrow weather and soil windows and little room for downtime, so an unnoticed fault in one row can be costly.

The 20|20 is Precision Planting’s in-cab display. It monitors and, with the right modules, controls the planter. Sabanto’s Vehicle Operating System (vOS) reads the planter data the 20|20 measures and checks it against limits the grower sets. In effect, it watches the same signals an operator would.

CEO Rupp says there is hardly any installation and that growers can handle it themselves.What the system reads

The data are read row by row. According to Rupp, vOS currently also reads population, downforce and liquid application rate from the 20|20. Seed singulation and vacuum pressure are in process, Rupp says. Growers with a Precision Planting Panorama subscription can also view 20|20 data remotely.

Growers set tolerances per row in vMC and can adjust all of them. If any parameter falls outside its tolerance, the tractor pauses. Rupp says Sabanto does not issue warnings: “We did not see the value in issuing warnings”, he says. “If things aren’t working, pause.” Sabanto’s press release says the operator is notified when a row falls outside tolerance.

Growers can supervise the work remotely.The tractor also pauses if it loses its connection to the 20|20 or to the internet during planting. Rupp calls that an error condition. When the tractor has paused, a remote operator can open the 20|20 view to diagnose the problem and make an adjustment, or call the tractor to the field edge for a closer look.

Installation and compatibility.

The practical hurdle is minor. The grower connects a CAN-bus cable to the Sabanto autonomy system. Rupp says there is hardly any installation and that growers can handle it themselves. The new system also works with older planters that already have a Gen 3 20|20, so growers who invested in the Precision Planting system in recent years can keep their existing setup.

Growers set tolerances per row in Vehicle Mission Control and can adjust all of them.For growers who already have a Sabanto system, the integration costs nothing, Rupp says. The same goes for new customers. Remote viewing through Panorama requires a subscription.

Sabanto positions the combination as a way to cut capital costs. The company believes smaller, cheaper equipment that runs longer beats bigger, more expensive iron, and it wants growers to keep the planter technology they already know.

Combined with a Sabanto-retrofitted tractor, the setup allows autonomous planting without an operator in the seat.Quint Pottinger of Affinity Farms in Kentucky, who uses the technology, says equipment costs have dropped in nearly every industry except farming. According to Pottinger, the combination of Sabanto and Precision Planting gives his farm financial runway and mental space.

Sabanto is not affiliated with or endorsed by Precision Planting or AGCO.

translationZh:
美国公司Sabanto宣布支持配备Precision Planting Gen 3 20|20系统的播种机。结合Sabanto改装的拖拉机，该配置可实现无人播种，驾驶座上无需操作员。农户可通过Sabanto的车辆任务控制（vMC）界面远程监督作业。该支持计划于2027年种植季推出。

“我希望看到一个农业技术更加开放的未来”，Sabanto创始人兼CEO Craig Rupp说道。他将其比作打印机：插上USB线，几分钟内就能工作。而在农业中，他说，让任何播种机和任何拖拉机协同工作远没有那么简单。Rupp将此次集成视为朝这个方向迈出的一步。

Sabanto表示，农户告诉他们，驾驶本身并不是自主播种的难点。更难的问题是，他们能否在没有人工盯守的情况下信任播种机。播种具有时间紧迫性，天气和土壤窗口狭窄，停机余地很小，因此某一行未被察觉的故障可能代价高昂。

20|20是Precision Planting的车内显示屏。它监测播种机，并在配备相应模块时控制播种机。Sabanto的车辆操作系统（vOS）读取20|20测量的播种机数据，并将其与农户设定的限值进行比对。实际上，它监测的是与操作员相同的信号。

CEO Rupp表示几乎无需安装，农户可以自行完成。

**系统读取哪些数据**

数据逐行读取。据Rupp介绍，vOS目前还从20|20读取种群密度、下压力和液体施用量。Rupp表示，种子单粒率和真空压力正在开发中。订阅了Precision Planting Panorama的农户还可以远程查看20|20数据。

农户在vMC中按行设置容差，并可调整所有容差。如果任何参数超出其容差范围，拖拉机将暂停。Rupp表示Sabanto不发出警告：“我们认为发出警告没有价值”，他说。“如果事情不正常，就暂停。”Sabanto的新闻稿称，当某一行超出容差时，操作员会收到通知。

农户可以远程监督作业。如果播种期间与20|20或互联网的连接丢失，拖拉机也会暂停。Rupp称这属于错误状态。拖拉机暂停后，远程操作员可以打开20|20视图诊断问题并进行调整，或呼叫拖拉机到田边近距离查看。

**安装与兼容性**

实际障碍很小。农户将CAN总线电缆连接到Sabanto自动驾驶系统。Rupp表示几乎无需安装，农户可以自行完成。新系统还可用于已配备Gen 3 20|20的旧播种机，因此近年来投资了Precision Planting系统的农户可以保留现有配置。

农户在车辆任务控制中按行设置容差，并可调整所有容差。对于已拥有Sabanto系统的农户，Rupp表示该集成免费。新客户同样如此。通过Panorama远程查看需要订阅。

Sabanto将这一组合定位为降低资本成本的方式。该公司认为，运行时间更长的小型廉价设备胜过更大更昂贵的铁家伙，并且希望农户保留他们已经熟悉的播种机技术。

肯塔基州Affinity Farms的Quint Pottinger使用了该技术，他说除农业外几乎所有行业的设备成本都在下降。据Pottinger称，Sabanto与Precision Planting的组合为他的农场提供了财务余地和心理空间。

Sabanto与Precision Planting或AGCO无关联，也未获其背书。
